# Windows x64 and ARM64 preview

An [unsigned Windows 11 preview installer](https://github.com/OpenProjectRoom/desktop/releases/tag/v0.9.78-windows-preview.1) is available for x64 and ARM64. The Windows 11 ARM64 Parallels smoke test covered installation, launch, demo Overview, Project Map, Services, Test Explorer, Settings, and project selection. Real project commands, API/MCP/data integrations, uninstall, and installed-to-installed updates still need a final Windows pass. The preview is separate from the signed, notarized Mac stable release and is not included in automatic release publication.

## Build and test on Windows

1. On Windows 10/11 x64 or ARM64, install Node.js 22 and Git. Clone this repository and run `npm ci`, `npm test`, and `npm run validate:config` in PowerShell. Benedikt's Parallels Windows 11 VM is ARM64; use the combined test installer to exercise its native payload.
2. Run `npm start`. Open the bundled working example, then an ordinary local project folder. Check the title bar, navigation, file reader, theme, and Project Chat. Dictation is currently macOS-only and is hidden on Windows.
3. In a disposable Node project, configure a service with `command: [npm, run, dev]`, a test with `command: [npm, test]`, and a local MCP server. Verify start, logs, stop, child-process exit, test output, MCP tool calls, and five-second CPU/RAM samples. Check Data Explorer, API Explorer, `.env` handling and OAuth separately. Shell scripts such as `./blackbox` are not Windows commands; the project must provide a Windows-compatible command.
4. Run `npm run package:win:app` for a local x64 unpacked build, or download the [unsigned preview installer](https://github.com/OpenProjectRoom/desktop/releases/tag/v0.9.78-windows-preview.1). The NSIS installer contains x64 and ARM64 payloads and selects the matching one. It has no publisher signature, so SmartScreen may warn. `npm run package:win` creates an unsigned local installer; only the release workflow can submit it for SignPath signing. Test a fresh install and uninstall on the same Windows computer before a stable release.

## One-time release setup

1. Apply to [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/apply.html). Its approval is discretionary. The [code signing policy](../../CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md) and [privacy notice](https://openprojectroom.com/privacy.html) must be public before applying. The SignPath Foundation certificate makes **SignPath Foundation** the Windows publisher, rather than Benedikt or OpenProjectRoom. Every signed release needs manual approval.
2. Once approved, configure a SignPath project linked to the public `OpenProjectRoom/desktop` repository and install the SignPath GitHub App with access limited to this repository. Use [the artifact configuration](../../signpath/windows-installer.xml) for the uploaded ZIP containing `Project-Room-Desktop-windows.exe`. Verify the installer metadata matches its declared product name and release version. Enable the release signing policy only for verified GitHub Actions builds.
3. Create a SignPath API token for the CI submitter and store it as the repository secret `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN`. Set repository Actions variables `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `SIGNPATH_PROJECT_SLUG`, `SIGNPATH_SIGNING_POLICY_SLUG`, and `SIGNPATH_ARTIFACT_CONFIGURATION_SLUG` to the values shown in SignPath. No PFX or private certificate key belongs in GitHub Actions.
4. After the final Windows validation, set `WINDOWS_SIGNING_READY=true`. Until then, normal version tags release only the Mac app; the unsigned Windows preview remains a separate prerelease. The Windows job uploads the unsigned installer as a GitHub workflow artifact, waits up to one hour for a human SignPath approval, verifies the returned Authenticode signature, rebuilds the blockmap and `latest.yml` from the **signed** bytes, and attaches those three files to the same stable GitHub release as Mac. If manual approval takes longer, rerun the failed Windows job after approval; never upload the unsigned installer to a stable release.
5. Install one signed Windows release, publish a second version, and verify that the in-app update banner downloads it and that **Restart to update** installs it. Check the installed app, uninstall path, installer signer, and `latest.yml` checksum on x64 and ARM64. Then switch the website and README Windows buttons from the explicit preview tag to the latest stable Windows asset.

The application form requests evidence of project reputation. Project Room is still young, so SignPath may decline or defer its Foundation certificate. The current Windows preview must stay clearly marked unsigned until approval and a successful signed release. The [SignPath GitHub integration documentation](https://docs.signpath.io/trusted-build-systems/github) describes its origin checks and signing action.

Every pull request also runs the source checks, builds an unsigned unpacked app and NSIS installer on `windows-latest`, and keeps the installer as a short-lived CI artifact. This verifies packaging, but it does not replace the manual install and updater test.
